- Model consistently overestimates early in the 30-day horizon, especially after recent spikes; reduce forecast by 1–2% for first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >45.0), model tends to overshoot and then overcorrect; apply a “cool-down” bias: reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per day post-spike.
- When sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high variance and overconfidence; apply a “mean-reversion” penalty: subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast if 3+ consecutive days show no sentiment change.
- Model underestimates late in horizon (last 10–15 days) when prices are trending down; adjust downward by 0.3–0.8% per day for downward momentum.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3+ consecutive days below 40.0), model tends to ignore it; apply a “reversion bias” rule: increase forecast by 0.2–0.5% for days following strong downward moves.
- For horizon >15 days, model often fails to account for event-driven volatility; if official event context is available (e.g., policy change, auction), adjust forecast ±1–2% based on event direction.
